messages:
alex: CI started failing on our monorepo after a tagged release change. go build errors with `unknown revision v2.1.0` when fetching an internal module referenced via a replace directive. Happened ~10:23am in the main pipeline.

maria: rough logs? which module path is failing? is this only in CI or locally too?

alex: only CI so far. local `go build ./...` works for me. CI shows: `go: github.com/acme/internal@v2.1.0: unknown revision v2.1.0`

alex: here's the minimal repro from CI agent: `GOCACHE=/tmp/cache go get github.com/acme/internal@v2.1.0` -> same unknown revision.

alex: go.mod snippet:```
module github.com/acme/service

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/acme/internal v2.1.0 // indirect
)

replace github.com/acme/internal => ../internal
```

samir: hmmm replace to a relative path is expected locally. CI checks out in a different workspace so replace can't resolve to ../internal. But that usually yields a file not found error, not unknown revision.

eng-oncall-bot: quick check: are we doing any retagging or force-push on v2.1.0 in the internal repo in last 24h? Commit: 7f3a2c was retagged per release-log.

maria: if the tag was deleted and re-created Git proxies/clients can report unknown revision depending on GOPROXY caching. Can you paste `GOPROXY` and `go env -w` output from CI?

alex: CI env: `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` and we don't set GONOSUMDB. Also found in CI logs a `403` from `sum.golang.org` for private module access.

support-ops: common pattern: relative `replace` works locally but in CI you need the actual version available to the proxy or a pseudo-version in go.mod. Workarounds: 1) publish a proper v2.1.0 tag on the module repo (no force-retag), 2) change replace to a module path with a pseudo-version (e.g., v0.0.0-yyyymmddhhmmss-commit) only for CI, or 3) configure CI to use `GOPRIVATE` so proxy is bypassed.

samir: action for eng: if the release tag was rewritten, re-create the tag pointing at the correct commit and push. If that's not possible, patch service go.mod to replace with `github.com/acme/internal v0.0.0-20240215123045-7f3a2c` (pseudo-version) and re-run CI.

maria: also double-check `module` path in the internal repo: v2 modules require `/v2` in the module path if they use semantic import versioning. If someone forgot that when tagging v2.1.0, proxy might reject it.

alex: copying minimal repro steps to the ticket: 1) checkout CI workspace, 2) run `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct go get github.com/acme/internal@v2.1.0`, 3) observe `unknown revision`.

samir: I'm going to try re-tagging locally and push the v2.1.0 tag (without force) and ping once done. If CI still fails, we'll flip CI to `GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme/*` as a temporary mitigation.

alex: thanks. tagging fix would be ideal, but adding `GOPRIVATE` in pipeline seems safest short term.

support-ops: noted. I've added `GOPRIVATE` to the pipeline sandbox and queued a rebuild.

eng-oncall-bot: rebuild started at 2055551240.

alex: rebuild succeeded in sandbox with `GOPRIVATE` set. CI main still failing until tag fix.

samir: pushed new tag v2.1.0 pointing at commit 7f3a2c without force (created v2.1.0-restore for trace). Please confirm main pipeline.

eng-oncall-bot: main pipeline rebuild triggered at 2055551244.

alex: main pipeline passed. closing for now. I'll follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems about avoiding retags and improving release checks. :white_check_mark:
